SEAM:READ_BASELINE.purpose: the baseline law and the shape of the period. readReportShape (pure) writes STATS.lake.prior_comparable (the period before is a baseline only when it holds at least a fifth of this period's signals and READ_BASELINE.MIN) and STATS.lake.shape per territory (n, share_pct, weeks, week_high, week_low over interior weeks, direction rising/holding/cooling from the two halves), at submit for a report and again at landing when a stored read lacks it. The report contract reads every count on its own shape when the prior is not comparable (never compares, never quotes the prior, never calls a territory new) and takes weekly figures from STATS, never from arithmetic. readMomentum: with no baseline the direction is the momentum, n_prior is withheld, share and high/low week ride on each territory. The number law admits every member of a serialized series ([273,336] counts 273 and 336). claudeParams sends temperature only to models below 5 (Sonnet 5 and Fable refuse it with a 400; the copy desk was skipped on every report until Oct 4); readProof sends none

SEAM:READ_BASELINE@page.purpose: rpComparable judges the baseline by the worker's flag or the same rule; without one the numbers band, the cards, the territories band and each territory's line read the share and the high and low week (rpShape) instead of a delta, the dashed prior average and the prior bars are withheld, the about cards say the record begins with this period

SEAM:READ_DESK.purpose: the copy desk in parts. The desk writes the whole read back as JSON, and at the live tier's pace a report takes six to eight minutes in one call, past the two-minute clock (Oct 4: claude_network on Issue 001; no read longer than a weekly was ever proofread). readProofParts (pure) splits a read longer than READ_PROOF.PART_CHARS by whole fields: a top-level array of objects longer than a part gives one part per element (the findings, the executive summary), every other key is grouped in order until a part fills; a read that fits is one call as before. readProofPool runs READ_PROOF.PARALLEL parts at once; readProofAssemble puts the edited parts back (a key the desk dropped keeps the original; the accept law judges the whole). One failed part skips the desk with the part named (part_k_of_n:reason) and the read stands; the receipt carries parts and what was spent even then

SEAM:READ_PRUNE.purpose: delete an old version of a read. POST /reads/delete {id} (admin): readPruneRefusal (pure) keeps three things, a cut that is on the stand or was (published), a cut whose batch is still out (compiling), and the newest cut of its window (a failed newer cut does not count), so a report window keeps its issue number, a weekly keeps the cut its stand issue was built from, and a child read a report built on stays readable; the row goes with the PDF rendered for it (meta.pdf.key in R2); the jobs ledger keeps its rows; read_pruned is logged

SEAM:READ_PRUNE@page.purpose: Delete this version on a cut that is not on the stand or compiling: a confirm names the cut and that the newer one stays, the house's refusal is explained in reader words (PRUNE_WHY), and a deleted cut returns to the library

note: planned seams live in /worker; they enter registry as they ship
